abstract: For every finite projective plane of order q>=2, its vertex incidence metric has an exact negative-type threshold as the unique p in (0,1) with sqrt(q)(3^p-1)=2^p. At the threshold the equality-space dimension is q^2+q, and the minimal Euclidean snowflake dimension is q^2+q+1.
integrity: Analytic proof uses projective-plane incidence identities, a full conditional spectral decomposition, and Schoenberg Gram rank. Standalone finite-field checker covers five orders; no claim of comprehensive computational proof for all planes.
limitations: Unit-weight graph vertex distances of existing finite projective planes only; no existence claim for arbitrary q; no classification of arbitrary symmetric incidence designs, or minimal-support optimality for the displayed equality.
title: Exact generalized roundness and critical Hilbert dimension of finite projective-plane incidence metrics
